Evidence: both invocations and their output, plus the byte-count delta.

The guidance an agent actually reads is corrected to name a safe form for consuming bp -o json (redirect to a file, pipe directly, or printf %s when re-emitting a variable) and to say plainly that echo $var is unsafe for JSON under zsh. Evidence: the diff, and the grep that finds any remaining echo-into-jq recipe in the same docs.

The FALSE-ABSENCE failure mode is stated wherever the recipe lives, not just the syntax fix: the corruption is uniform across rows, so it presents as empty or missing data rather than as an error about the pipe. Evidence: the wording as landed.

content.value:
Every agent in this campaign runs zsh and parses bp … -o json. The idiom j=$(bp task get "$id" -o json); echo "$j" | jq … SILENTLY CORRUPTS the JSON, and the way it fails is the dangerous part: it fails UNIFORMLY, on every row, so it reads as a property of the data rather than of the pipe.

SCOPE, measured per shell rather than assumed — this is NOT a zsh-only fault, and it does NOT affect bash:

    shell   echo interprets backslash escapes?   echo "$json" | jq -r .ok
    bash    NO                                   true            SAFE
    sh      YES                                  parse error     CORRUPTS
    zsh     YES                                  parse error     CORRUPTS

(The first draft of this row said "under zsh". That was the shell I hit it in, not the boundary. /bin/sh — dash — corrupts identically, and bash does not corrupt at all.)

THE MEASUREMENT, one row, one capture, three writers, under zsh:

    j=$(env -u BARKPARK_TOKEN bp task get gr-blk-accent-scenario-sweep -o json)

    echo "$j"        | jq -r '.doc.content.lifecycle_status'
      -> jq: parse error: Invalid string: control characters from U+0000 through
         U+001F must be escaped at line 9, column 310
    printf '%s' "$j" | jq -r '.doc.content.lifecycle_status'   -> done
    print -r -- "$j" | jq -r '.doc.content.lifecycle_status'   -> done

    printf bytes=9917   echo bytes=9908   delta=-9

A JSON string carrying \n, \t or \" is TWO characters on the wire; an escape-interpreting echo collapses each to one real control character inside the string, which is exactly what RFC 8259 forbids unescaped. Nine bytes vanished from this row.

BP IS NOT AT FAULT. Written straight to a file the same rows are valid JSON and jq reads them. Checked on three rows (gr-blk-accent-scenario-sweep, task-9f09b84ae8248a71, task-561ac06ea4ebb607): zero raw control characters below 0x20 other than the trailing newline.

THE REPO IS ALSO LARGELY NOT AT FAULT, checked rather than assumed. One *.sh outside .claude/worktrees/ uses the pattern — scripts/bp-vercel-quick-setup.sh:243 — and its shebang is #!/usr/bin/env bash, so it is SAFE and needs no change. The live surface is (a) an agent's own ad-hoc shell, which is zsh here, and (b) .claude/skills/session/SKILL.md lines 194, 205 and 223, which are recipes an agent PASTES into that shell.

WHY IT MATTERS MORE THAN A STYLE NOTE. I hit this while AUDITING MY OWN CLOSES — checking that every criterion I stamped cites a merge commit that is genuinely an ancestor of origin/main. The loop used echo "$j" | jq, and seven of eight rows printed a blank lifecycle, 0/0 criteria and no sha in evidence. Read at face value that says my stamps are empty and my closes are hollow. Re-run through a tolerant parser, all eight rows are done, fully met, every cited commit ON-MAIN. A uniform verdict is the signature of a broken instrument, and this one manufactures a false ABSENCE — the class inspection never catches.

REMEDY. Name a safe form wherever the recipe lives: redirect to a file, pipe bp … -o json | jq … directly, or use printf '%s' / print -r -- when a variable must be re-emitted. Say plainly that echo "$var" is unsafe for JSON in any escape-interpreting shell, and that bash's safety is not a defence because the same line pasted into a zsh session corrupts.

tags.rationale: A shell idiom used across the campaign to read the ledger silently corrupts the payload and reports the damage as missing data.
The affected payload is bp task get -o json, which every lead and worker parses; bp itself emits valid JSON and is not at fault.

doc.title: echo $json | jq corrupts every bp -o json payload in zsh AND sh (not bash) and manufactures a uniform false ABSENCE
